text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA

- The government expects that a redenomination of the Russian rouble, which will be carried from January 1, 1998, will encourage the "de-dollarisation" of Russia's economy, a top banking official is quoted as saying.
- Russians spent about 20.8 percent of their earnings on buying hard currency in the last six months, according to official statistics.

- The head of the Russian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Alexiy II, is planning to cooperate with President Boris Yeltsin in the amending a draft law on religion which has been criticised for infringing the rights of non-Orthodox communities.
- American automaker Ford is said to be holding talks on opening a range of joint ventures in Russia.
ROSSISKAYA GAZETA
- Russians won't lose anything, the government daily promises over the planned redenomination of the rouble.
- The government still has full control over the situation at Svyazinvest holding after the recent share sale, says Alfred Kokh, head of the State Privatization Committee.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Redenomination of the Russian rouble may mean a speeding up of the emission of more money, says the paper.
- An important precedent has been created in Russia when, at the request of the prosecutor-general's pffoice, the government suspends the auction of 38 percent of the Norilsk Nickel shares.
- St Petersburg authorities are planning to sell about 60 percent of shares in the Astoria Hotel as a first step to remove hotels from the city budget.
SEVODNYA
- It is not yet clear what will happen to bank deposits after three zeros are knocked off Russian roubles beginning next year, says the paper.
- Federal budget losses may grow if the parliament drags out the passage of a new Tax Code, says Deputy Finance Minister Sergei Shatalov.
- The most important launch in the history of Baikonur is due to take place on Tuesday, says the paper before the relief space crew blasts off, watched by top defence and security officials.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The redenomination of the rouble poses big questions about the overall aim of costly reforms, says the paper.
- Rem Vyakhirev, the head of Gazprom, maintains top position in a list of Russia's most influential businessmen, according to an independent survey.

- Critical remarks made at the weekend by presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky about Russian Public Television, which ignored President Boris Yeltsin's activity in the covarage of the day's events, are comparable to the situation in Belarus, where independent journalists are persecuted by local administration, says the paper.
KOMSOMOLSKAYA PRAVDA
- Former defence minister Pavel Grachev expects to get a new job this autumn. The paper publishes Grachev's first interview since his resignation.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- "Sugar fever" has swept Moscow because of rumours that Ukraine is planning to reduce sugar exports to Russia. Sugar prices have jumped 15-20 percent, the paper says.
- Space Mission Control and a radio channel are carrying out a joint project to support Russian cosmonauts on the Mir space station by broadcasting their favourite music and songs.
--Tatayna Ustinova, Moscow newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
